summary: Patch adds a hardcoded non-standard `Proxy-Connection: keep-alive` header inside `HTTPProxyAuth.__call__`, but the reported bug uses `proxies=` dict where proxy auth flows through `rebuild_proxies`/`proxy_headers`, not `HTTPProxyAuth`, so this code path is not even exercised by the repro. Wrong location, non-standard header, and unconditional injection make it a fragile, likely non-fixing change.

issues.description: `HTTPProxyAuth` is a manual auth class; the reported scenario (`requests.get(url, proxies=proxies)`) sets `Proxy-Authorization` via `rebuild_proxies`/`HTTPAdapter.proxy_headers`, not through `HTTPProxyAuth.__call__`. The edited path is not on the default proxy flow, so the change likely does not resolve the actual 407 for the reported use case.

Root cause is the CPython 3.8.12 backport affecting tunneled HTTPS proxy connections at the urllib3/http.client layer. Injecting a header only when a user explicitly opts into `HTTPProxyAuth` leaves the common `proxies=` path (the one in the report) unfixed.
`Proxy-Connection` is a non-standard/deprecated hop-by-hop header; hardcoding `keep-alive` unconditionally is brittle and may conflict with connection handling for proxies that don't expect it.
Appears special-cased to satisfy a repro that directly invokes `HTTPProxyAuth`, rather than fixing the general proxy-auth path that the issue describes.
